description: Behavioral feature contract for ML-based ransomware detection. Defines the exact features consumed by the ML model, their types, sources, and semantics.

classification.label_description: 0 = normal system behavior within the observation window. 1 = behavioral pattern associated with ransomware-like activity within the observation window.

ml_features.name: total_events
ml_features.description: Total number of events from all monitors within the observation window.
ml_features.ransomware_relevance: Ransomware generates abnormally high total event volume due to rapid file operations combined with process and network activity.

ml_features.name: file_created
ml_features.description: Number of file creation events within the observation window.
ml_features.ransomware_relevance: Ransomware may create encrypted copies of files or ransom note files. High creation rate from a single process is suspicious.

ml_features.name: file_modified
ml_features.description: Number of file modification events within the observation window.
ml_features.ransomware_relevance: Core ransomware behavior — encrypting files in place registers as modification. Rapid modification of many files is a primary indicator.

ml_features.name: file_deleted
ml_features.description: Number of file deletion events within the observation window.
ml_features.ransomware_relevance: Some ransomware deletes original files after creating encrypted copies. Bulk deletion paired with creation is suspicious.

ml_features.name: file_renamed
ml_features.description: Number of file rename events within the observation window.
ml_features.ransomware_relevance: Ransomware commonly renames files with new extensions (e.g., .encrypted, .locked). Bulk renaming is a strong behavioral signal.

ml_features.name: unique_files_modified
ml_features.description: Number of distinct files that were modified within the observation window.
ml_features.ransomware_relevance: Key discriminator — ransomware targets many different files. A legitimate process may modify the same file repeatedly, but ransomware spreads across unique targets.

ml_features.name: process_events
ml_features.description: Total number of process-related events within the observation window.
ml_features.ransomware_relevance: Ransomware may spawn child processes for parallel encryption or use helper processes. Abnormal process churn combined with file activity is suspicious.

ml_features.name: network_events
ml_features.description: Total number of network-related events within the observation window.
ml_features.ransomware_relevance: Ransomware may communicate with C2 servers, exfiltrate data before encryption, or download encryption keys. Network activity concurrent with file operations is suspicious.

ml_features.name: established_connections
ml_features.description: Number of successfully established network connections within the observation window.
ml_features.ransomware_relevance: Active outbound connections during file encryption activity may indicate C2 communication or data exfiltration.

ml_features.name: unique_remote_ips
ml_features.description: Number of distinct remote IP addresses contacted within the observation window.
ml_features.formula: count(distinct remote IPs from network events)
ml_features.ransomware_relevance: Contacting many unique remote IPs may indicate scanning, C2 failover, or distributed exfiltration. Combined with high file activity, this strengthens the ransomware signal.

excluded_features.name: file_events
excluded_features.explanation: This is the sum of file_created + file_modified + file_deleted + file_renamed. Including both the aggregate and its components introduces multicollinearity without adding information. The individual components are more informative for the model because they distinguish between different file operation types, which have different ransomware relevance.

excluded_features.name: suspicious_indicators
excluded_features.explanation: This feature is derived from the rule-based detection engine (e.g., 10 unique files modified in 10 seconds triggers a suspicious indicator). Using it as ML input would mean the model learns to replicate the rule rather than discovering independent behavioral patterns. The ML model must demonstrate value beyond the existing rules. See suspicious_indicators_decision.md for full rationale.

proposed_future_features.name: file_modification_rate
proposed_future_features.rationale: Normalizes file modification count by window duration, enabling comparison across different window sizes.

proposed_future_features.name: file_ops_per_process
proposed_future_features.rationale: Ransomware typically shows high file operations concentrated in few processes. This ratio captures that concentration.

proposed_future_features.name: rename_to_modify_ratio
proposed_future_features.rationale: Ransomware that encrypts-then-renames shows a high rename-to-modify ratio compared to normal editing which rarely renames.

proposed_future_features.name: delete_to_create_ratio
proposed_future_features.rationale: Ransomware that creates encrypted copies then deletes originals shows balanced delete/create counts. Normal behavior rarely shows this pattern.

proposed_future_features.name: network_file_ratio
proposed_future_features.rationale: Captures the relationship between network and file activity. Exfiltration-before-encryption shows network activity proportional to file operations.

compatibility_notes.mapping: ML preprocessing selects the 10 ML_FEATURE_COLUMNS from the full 12-feature output of feature_extractor.py
